characters.name: Per
characters.description: The youngest son, poor and ragged at first, who becomes “Sir Per” through the cat’s schemes and ends up ruling a realm.
characters.look: A gangly, gentle young man of about nineteen with a long neck, long arms, a kind oval face, soft brown eyes, a straight nose, a shy smile and chestnut hair tied back in a short ponytail. characters.name: The King
characters.description: A proud ruler delighted by lavish gifts, then irritated by Per’s boasting, who follows him to see the supposed splendor for himself.
characters.look: A short, very fat king of about sixty with a round, shiny bald head, bulging cheeks, a red nose, small beady eyes, a grumpy look and a huge drooping grey walrus moustache that hides his mouth. A small gold crown sits right on top of his bald head. He wears a long purple wool robe with a spotted ermine collar, stretched tight over his enormous belly, a wide gold belt, white stockings and pointed red leather shoes.

characters.name: The Troll of the Castle
characters.description: The monstrous owner of the shining castle, undone when the cat tricks him into turning toward the rising sun.
characters.look: A colossal old troll about four times a man's height, round-shouldered and heavy, covered all over in long, matted, oatmeal-beige fur like a giant unshorn ram, with heather and twigs caught in it. Two round yellow eyes glow like lanterns above a big potato nose, and his broad, soft mouth shows two blunt buck teeth. He has little round ears, great grey hands like stone, a long cow's tail with a tuft at the end and broad, hairy bare feet.

characters.name: The Princess
characters.description: The cat’s true self: a princess the troll had bewitched. Freed at last, she lets Sir Per decide whether to make her his queen.
characters.look: A graceful young woman of about nineteen with a small pointed chin, high cheekbones, almond-shaped green-gold eyes like a cat's, a little upturned nose and very long, straight golden hair falling to her knees, with one silver-grey streak at her left temple. She wears a dove-grey silk gown with snow-white cuffs, a white lace collar and fine silver embroidery at the hem, and a thin silver circlet on her brow.

The enormous Troll has stood listening all night and still stands with his back to the low wooded ridge, where the rim of the rising sun is just breaking over the trees in a blaze of gold. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Troll: A colossal old troll about four times a man's height, round-shouldered and heavy, covered all over in long, matted, oatmeal-beige fur like a giant unshorn ram, with heather and twigs caught in it. Two round yellow eyes glow like lanterns above a big potato nose, and his broad, soft mouth shows two blunt buck teeth. He has little round ears, great grey hands like stone, a long cow's tail with a tuft at the end and broad, hairy bare feet.
- the Dressed-up Cat: A clever, dignified grey tabby cat, a little larger than an ordinary farm cat, with dark silver-grey stripes, four snow-white paws, a white chest, big green-gold eyes, long white whiskers and her old faded red leather collar, now dressed for visiting: a small red hat with a curling white feather set at a jaunty angle between her ears, and a little moss-green cloak fastened at her throat with a tiny brass clasp. She walks and sits upright and proud, her striped tail held high.

Setting:
- the Silver Castle: A great castle made all of polished silver, with slender towers and steep silver roofs, standing on a green rise in a wide summer landscape and shining so brightly in the sun that it hurts the eyes. In front of it, three tall arched gates stand one behind the other across the road: the first of brass, the second of silver and the third of gold, each between two thick stone gateposts. Across a meadow opposite the gates rises a low wooded ridge.

Story world: Old rural Norway in high summer. Per's parents' tiny grey log cottage stands empty at the edge of a spruce forest. The King's manor is a cluster of dark log buildings with turf roofs and carved gables, with a great hall and a big, smoky kitchen hung with copper kettles. From there a long country road winds over green hills, past pastures of long-wooled sheep, brindled cows and horses, to the Silver Castle, where everything inside is gold. The pot is a round black iron pot, the griddle a big, flat, round iron griddle with a handle. The silver spoon, silver ladle and silver cup come from the King's table. Sir Per drives a small gilded carriage drawn by four white horses; the King follows in a big dark-red carriage with six courtiers on horseback.

This story's season, light and colours: High summer at haymaking time: deep-blue skies with towering white clouds, lush green hills, hay meadows full of buttercups and a dazzling sun that sets silver and gold blazing. Accents: dove-grey, scarlet, moss green and glittering gold.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape.
